title: Already gone
prompt: It is 10:40 ET. Read the chart and decide.

intro.beginner: A good move started over an hour ago. Look at how far price has travelled from where the trade would have been taken.
intro.advanced: 10:40 ET. The move is an hour old. What's left?

whyNot.label: buying at market
whyNot.why: The edge was in the gap the displacement left, more than 150 points down. Buying here pays for the whole move, puts the stop a full leg away, and leaves almost nothing before the previous day high.

whyNot.label: shorting the extension
whyNot.why: Extended isn't reversed. Nothing has swept or displaced down, and the higher timeframe is up.

reference.summary: A valid long that was taken, or missed, an hour ago. Price is extended and sitting just under the previous day high. The decision now isn't to chase: it's to wait, with a resting order at the gap, for the retrace that comes.

bias.why: Higher highs and higher lows on the Daily and 4H; the move since the open is the trend continuing.

decision.why: Chasing is the mistake. Waiting, or a resting limit order in the original gap, is the position; passing entirely is defensible but gives up a real second chance.

take.why: Not at this price. The setup is the gap, not the high.

draw.why: The previous day high is the pool, and price is close to it.

location.why: Price is extended far above the gap.

next_objective.why: Price was drawn to the previous day high (21,046.25); it also traded to the unfilled gap at 20,995.5 to 21,014.75 on the way, which makes those defensible too. The question is where price was likely to be pulled, not what the next candle would do. A previous-day extreme is also a pool of buy-side or sell-side liquidity, so that answer is right on the side, if less exact.

annotations.label: 5m bullish FVG from the displacement
annotations.why: The entry area, an hour and 150+ points back. A resting limit here is the trade; a market order here and now is not.
annotations.decisionNote: Patience with a resting order, or no trade. Not a market order.

annotations.label: 5m order block under the gap
annotations.why: The alternative area from the same origin.

annotations.label: Previous day high 21,046.25
annotations.why: The draw, and price is already close to it: which is why chasing has nothing left to pay.
annotations.decisionNote: Reward left from here is tiny against a stop a full leg below.

annotations.label: Overnight low 20,815
annotations.why: The sell-side liquidity swept an hour ago.

confluences.label: The overnight low was swept an hour ago
confluences.why: Context for the gap, not a reason to buy now.

confluences.label: Price is more than a full leg above the entry area
The origin gap is still unfilled below
Previous day high is close above
confluences.why: Little room left for a market entry.

confluences.label: Strong momentum right now
confluences.why: Momentum into the draw is the end of the move, not a place to start one.

confluences.label: "It keeps going"
confluences.why: A move that's already happened isn't a setup.

trade.confirmationLabel: the displacement that closed above the last 5m high

lookFor: If the entry area is more than a leg behind you, the trade is gone. Wait for price to come back to it or move on.
A resting limit order at the gap is a patient way to stay in a trade you missed.
Check the room: the distance to the draw must justify the distance to the stop.

provenance.note: Constructed price path, not market history.
